**ACCEPT** — PR #12302. ⚠️ **But holding the flip on one specific CI job**, see the bottom.

All three ruled steps landed in order, and each of the three fences I set was actually honoured rather than nodded at.

### Step 1 — the universality claim was measured, and it **holds**

I dispatched this with *"expect this to find something"* and it did not. That is a legitimate outcome **because it was measured**: the case-set's *"the six accepted types compile everywhere"* was run on live PostgreSQL 16.13 (initdb'd locally), all eight executed cases answered the case-set's row ids, **and the case-set was not narrowed**. The fence was "⛔ do not narrow the case-set to make the suite pass" — nothing was narrowed, so the green means what it says.

⭐ **One design call worth naming**, because it resists a tempting mistake: the door-refusal half stays declared **once** rather than per cell, on the grounds that `parseFilterAST` is a pure platform function upstream of every driver — *"running it per cell would measure one thing three times and report the repetition as coverage."* That is exactly right, and it is the failure mode this whole card family exists to prevent: a coverage number inflated by repetition. A new bind block covers the layer that *can* speak for the un-provisioned cell (every accepted type binds on all three dialect clients without a server).

### Step 2 — verified **by operator**, which is what I fenced

I wrote: *"Measure by operator, not by file. If the matrix suite does not actually cover the same operators this one does, marking it hides a real gap."* Measured off the exported case data: **the seven text operators this suite reaches are exactly the seven `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` reaches**, and `sql-driver-text-case-conformance.test.ts` runs that table once per cell. Coverage overlaps ⇒ the marking hides nothing. #6518's dialect divergence stays covered.

### Step 3 — promoted, and hardened beyond the ask

`DIALECT_LEDGER` is empty, the census gained a per-cell `MATRIXED` invariant, and the dialect line moved **8 of 9 → 9 of 9**.

⭐ Better than ruled: **a ledger row deliberately does NOT clear `MATRIXED`**, narrowing the escape hatch a ledger normally opens — stated in the ledger comment, in the error message, **and pinned by self-test**. A ledger that could silence the invariant it was created to retire would have quietly re-created #12014.

### Before/after on the gate it changed — exactly as demanded

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| covered cells | 45 | **45** — unchanged, *and that is the point*: no CONSUMED answer moves |
| dialect line | 8 of 9 | **9 of 9** |
| DIALECT ledger | 2 | **0** |
| matrix suites | 5 | 6 |
| named cells | 0 | 1 |

Every movement is this PR's own doing, not a pre-existing green — which is the specific trap I named at dispatch.

### The ablation has a third leg that earns its place

- clean → exit 0, `9 of 9`, 0 `MATRIXED`
- mutated → exit 1, exactly 1 `MATRIXED` naming `FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPE_CASES`, **0 `DIALECTED`** (the suite still declares honestly — that is the claim being isolated)
- ⭐ mutated **+ `MATRIXED`'s `errors.push` deleted** → exit 0 printing `8 of 9` — **#12014's original defect reproduced with a real mutation**

That third leg is what proves the new invariant is the thing doing the work, not a coincidence of the surrounding change.

Anchored **single-line** greps with `^…$` on both edited lines (removed 0 / injected 1) — my `grep -cF` counts-lines-not-occurrences warning was heeded. Implementation committed first (#12204). Restore verified by `git hash-object` == HEAD blob, clean porcelain, census green again. No dist involved, and that is **stated rather than skipped**: the census is a pure node script reading source text, so there is no artifact for a mutation to fail to reach.

`check:type-check-debt` was **not** run and is declared **NOT MEASURED** (needs the built closure) rather than quietly omitted. It runs in CI.

### ⚠️ Why I am not flipping this yet

The dev declared one gap honestly rather than glossing it:

> the **MySQL cell could not be executed locally** (mysqld exits 1 with zero output; no Docker daemon) … but CI's `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job runs the whole driver-sql package with both URLs and `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`, so this converted suite's MySQL cell **WILL** execute there. That job is where a MySQL comparand-type divergence would surface, and **it is worth watching on this PR**.

That is precisely right, and it is an instruction to me. Step 1 converted a suite from one dialect to three; the MySQL third has **never been executed**. If a comparand type does not compile on MySQL, that job is where it appears — and it would be a **real finding**, not a flake, and not something to re-run past.

⇒ Holding the flip until `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` completes on this PR. It is `in_progress` now with no failures elsewhere. ⛔ If it goes red on a comparand-type case, that is a genuine dialect divergence and the card's premise changes — I will not treat it as infrastructure noise.

## Hold released — the MySQL cell ran in CI and **passed**

`Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` on PR #12302 completed **success** at 17:17:43.

That was the one job that could have turned this card's result around. The dev converted `sql-driver-comparand-type-conformance.test.ts` from one dialect to three but could only execute the Postgres cell locally (no mysqld, no Docker), so the MySQL third had **never been run** — and the case-set's own prose claims the six accepted comparand types *"compile everywhere"*.

⇒ That claim is now measured on **all three** dialects rather than asserted on one. No divergence, so nothing to narrow and nothing to fork back on.

Flipped to ready and auto-merge SQUASH armed.
